blurb: Files on a Branch. Names match the tools agents already know. Reads answer content, not revisions; each write answers its Commit.
reasons: Why reads answer no Commit: an agent asked for content. The Commit it read is noise in every result and tempts a guard the agent didn't ask for. To guard a write, pass --expected with the head from branch get or the last write; to read a fixed revision, pass --at.
Why --at on every read: read, stat, list, glob, grep, history and blame all pin a Commit the same way, so file stat … --at 7a0b11c2 reads a file as it was.

Why file.diff is gone: it compared two files, each at its own Branch or Commit. One path between two Commits is now commit diff … --path; comparing two different paths is dropped, and so is its line-ownership option (file blame answers ownership).
Why the single writes stay: agents use them as tools named for the action. Folding them into file.apply would save six calls and cost ease of use.
Why -m and --expected on every write: each write is one Commit, so each takes its message and the one head guard.
